answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (report.py output, read-only — no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

RECORDS & ANOMALIES
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20), spanning 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 detections above Mc)
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5) — this is the calibrated probability:
  b      Sigma      P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0    -5.449     0.0001198      5.236e-06                   0.03719
  0.73   -5.319     0.004922       0.0002155                   0.2809
  0.65   -5.281     0.01474        0.0006484                   0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts) — this is the upper bound, not calibrated:
  b 0.9849, Sigma -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated LBNL-catalogue estimate gives P(Mw>=5.5) per year of ~1.2e-4 (b=1.0) to ~1.5e-2 (b=0.65), whereas the DAS-based upper bound of 0.07842/yr over-counts because its magnitudes are uncalibrated and every detection is treated as an event at or above Mc. A Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is therefore unlikely under the calibrated estimate but cannot be excluded given the DAS-based upper bound.
